- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS expenditure by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing same-day GP access for urgent needs, universal NHS dentist access (£3bn annually by 2030), increased staff pay, and £1.5bn for public health restoration. Mental health services would receive equal priority, with 28-day access to therapies. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

## Social Care
A £20bn annual investment would fund free personal care modelled on Scotland's system, improved carer pay and career structures, and an additional £3bn for children's social care. Disability benefits would increase by 5%.

## Housing
Plans include 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a £29bn five-year home insulation programme. All new homes would meet Passivhaus standards with solar panels and heat pumps.

## Energy and Climate
The party proposes ending new oil and gas licences, removing fossil fuel subsidies, and achieving 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030. Nuclear development would cease. A carbon tax starting at £120/tonne would rise to £500/tonne within ten years. Community ownership thresholds for renewable infrastructure would be mandated, with £4bn annually for workforce transition training.

## Economy and Taxation
Average £40bn annual green investment is proposed. Water companies and railways would return to public ownership. Tax reforms include a 1-2% wealth tax on assets above £10m, aligning capital gains with income tax rates, and removing the upper National Insurance earnings limit—estimated to raise £50-70bn annually.

## Workers' Rights
Proposals include a £15 minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, moving toward a four-day week, and equal rights for gig economy workers.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and the five-week benefit wait would end. Long-term plans include Universal Basic Income.

## Environment and Nature
A Rights of Nature Act would grant legal personhood to nature. Targets include 30% of land and sea protected by 2030, rewetting all peatland, and banning harmful pesticides. Water companies would be nationalised.

## Education
Proposals include £8bn school investment, £2bn teacher pay uplift, £5bn for SEND provision, scrapped tuition fees, restored maintenance grants, and academies returned to local authority control.

## Transport
£10bn annual rail and bus subsidies would fund free bus travel for under-18s. Railways would be publicly owned. Petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027, with £2.5bn annually for cycling and walking infrastructure.

## Democracy
Proposals include proportional representation, votes at 16, an elected second chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022's voter ID requirements.

## Immigration
The party advocates ending the hostile environment, creating safe asylum routes, abolishing income requirements for spousal visas, and permitting asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## Foreign Policy
The manifesto calls for an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty, and increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI by 2033.

## Justice
Proposals include ending routine stop-and-search, making misogyny a hate crime, presumption against custodial sentences under two years, and £11bn Ministry of Justice investment.
